newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market climbed to small gains at the close on Friday as dealers were squaring books ahead of the second round of the French election Sunday.
"The market has not yet completely discounted the possibility that the French left wing can gain a full majority," a dealer at BNP in Madrid said.
The general consensus was the left would take power from the ruling centre-right coalition, but dealers were cautious after polls proved to be unreliable only one week ago.
A dealer here in Madrid added that if the right wins the market is likely to rally on Monday.
They said that the less market-friendly outcome would be a minority government backed by the far left.

Earlier on Friday, right before the close, German Bundesbank board member Reimut Jochimsen scared the markets by saying the gold revaluation plan increased the probability of higher interest rates overall.
"His remarks were really strong. But this afternoon people are thinking more about France's election," another said.
The Spanish 10-year spread versus Bunds fell to 75 basis points versus 78 basis points earlier this morning, at the same closing level of Thursday.
The long-bond future found strong support at the day's low of 114.25, while it ended above the previous resistance at 114.75, leaving doors open to a possible rally on Monday.
"I think the market has corrected enough already, but on Monday our moves will hinge on the French result," another dealer added.

Next week, possible weakness could come from the Treasury's monthly refunding. The Treasury will auction three-, five-, 10-, and 15-year bonds as well as six-month bills on Tueday and Wednesday next week.
